Gwijo Squad : War cries to remember

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Its a movement that hopes to inspire the nation through Springbok fanaticism and song, We join the Gwijo Squad in song and dance , as they push the Springboks to victory!y

Unique Selling Point:
A movement is born through iGwijo ...In a stadium built for crowds, the Springboks A faced the French Barbarians in a game that’s been getting our nation off their couches for decades. Rugby’s reputation precedes it and galvanizes fans across the globe with unwavering support, chanting war cries that fuel the players on the field with deafening roars when any of our heroes puts the ball beyond the try line. The problem with this match at Moses Mabida was staggering: the stadium was empty.

Chulumanco Macingwane contacted a few friends with his concern that such a tangible opportunity to connect people with their country’s sports people was being lost. A week later, 35 people united in Soweto to add their voices to a game that saw the same two teams face each other — but to a way more enthusiastic soundtrack…

The Gwijo Squad was born.

With most members hailing from the Eastern Cape, the Gwijo Squad is a sports fans movement with the vision and purpose of stimulating inclusive involvement for supporters around the country across rugby, cricket and netball, by igniting a cohesive energy that unifies people through song.

They believe that transformation and winning are not mutually exclusive.
They are now 920* strong — and growing!

Script:


Script : Gwijo Squad

Opening V/O : It's a love affair like no other…South Africans and their beloved Bokke!

V/O From the darkest of days….

V/O …to the proudest moments…

V/O And ultimately reaching the pinnacle of world rugby… Springbok fans have always been there…

Opening LINK Derek: It's no secret; South Africa is a rugby-crazy country with some of the most fanatical supporters in the world, but I am joining group of fans who are taking it to another level.


V/O In a country characterised by its differences, and a sport defined by its past, these passionate rugby fans, who call themselves the ‘Gwijo Squad’ are on a mission.

V/O To create a more inclusive sporting culture, where stadiums become multicultural, and South Africans unify through the power of a homegrown offering.… isiXhosa anthems called Amagwijo’…


V/O So what is ‘Amagwijo’?

Upsound Sbu Mjikelo :It's very difficult to explain iGwijo. It's not simply a song. It's not a chant. It's not a war cry. It is emotional.

V/O Sport24 Deputy-Editor and Author Sibusiso Mjikeliso says “Amagwijo are close to his heart.
Upsound Sbu Mjikelo : Rugby in the Eastern Cape and parts of the Western Cape is has got a huge cultural place in black people's society, it's not merely a sport,It amalgamates with Xhosa culture, with amagwijo , so you find yourself in the rugby field singing Amagwijo , cheering your team on .I mean schools that were you know,were exclusively white students,now they sing amagwijo when the first team is playing , to the point were they are part of the schoolwar cry.

V/O Its match day…The Springboks are taking on a familiar foe - the All Blacks… at the Emirates Airline park and I am invited to a prematch braai by one of the members.
Upsound :00:08:04:28 - 00:08:29:28 We come from all shapes, as you can see, different sizes, genders, etcetera. we don't exclude anybody. Your only entrance criteria is that you show up.
Upsound Derek question: Will I have to improve my Xhosa…?
Upsound 00:08:31:06 - 00:08:44:18:You want to support the Springboks, stand with the guys, have a listen, within 20 minutes you'll have one or two songs and off we go.

V/O It all started back in 2017, when Sijadu Mzozonyana and a group of friends attended a Springbok A match against the French Barbarians in Durban.

Upsound Sijadu : In watching that game there was just no support. So our chairman and founder Chulumanco Macingwane and his wife Nandi, they contacted a number of us.They said there’s another game in Soweto. We all put money together. We hired a bus and we experienced incredible magic…

V/O The clash was held at Orlando Stadium.

Upsound Sijadu : But when we unified in song, we filled the stadium. The players on the field. were incredibly lifted by hearing support in their mother tongue. We saw that there's a different avenue of inclusivity and an opportunity for us to support not just the players, but to bring people with us in the sport.

V/O And when Eastern Cape-born Siya Kolisi stepped onto the pitch for the first time as captain of the Springboks, the Gwijo squad didn’t miss the opportunity to give him a uniquely South African experience…

V/O … now years later, nothing has changed…
Upsound Sijadu :00:09:34:24 - 00:10:05:15>The reason why our captain is able to connect with us is because he understands where he comes from and where he comes from he knows amagwijo and what they mean.
V/O: And he’s not the only one… I spoke to the team's most experienced waterboy, former coach Rassie Erasmus, who once went the extra mile to become a certified member of the squad….



Upsound Rassie: I'm from Despatch in Eastern Cape I obviously know about the dancing and they do it when they’re happy and when they’re sad. They’ve got many reasons.

Upsound Derek:When did you first hear of the Gwijo squad?

Upsound Rassie Erasmus : We were in a meeting and then Siya explained to me and a few of the guys and I had to chat to two other guys from other backgrounds and we said, But let's allow everybody to express themselves and then I got to understand .I go into the hotel window and they would be in the foyer.


Travelling sequence :

V/O With kick off a few hours away, it was finally time to join the rest of the Gwijo Squad.

Upsound Derek : How are we doing for time ?

Upsound Sijadu: We are a bit late

V/O luckily the party bus had not left without us...

Upsound : Pep talk 0:17: Derek Watts is here, You guys remember him from Generations right ?

Derek : No voice

Pep talk 0:45 Let's go with the Gwijo spirit Let's go there and have a Jol…Masambe Nono !

V/O With Igwijo ringing through the bus … I was starting to feel the Gees or as the young ones say… iVibes.
].

Upsound Derek What made you join the Gwijo Squad

Upsound Happy: I hate when they sing Ole, Ole. It's not a South African song, Let's sing a South African song at the rugby games.

V/O Not confident in my ‘Gwijo skills’ yet, I had to do some fine-tuning.

Upsound Sijadu: 00:53 When You hear the song is captivating and the song is lifting, everybody will chant Kubo

Upound Derek : Kubo !

Upsound: Sijadu: The second word is Halala

Upound Derek : Halala ,Kubo , Halala.


V/O The big moment had arrived… and the Gwijo Squad was not letting up.

Links Derek: Link going into the stadium: Its 4 o'clock, and our until kick-off, the Gwijo squad is just starting off, and I am dog tired.

V/O Just a week before, The boks had trounced the All Blacks in Mbombela and the Gwijo Squad were still in high spirits…

Match short sequence :

V/O The Stage was set.

Upsound Derek : Kubo !

V/O For over 30 minutes it was an onslaught from the New Zealanders

V/O But Amagwijo still echoed across the stadium

V/O But despite a late rally by the Boks

V/O And a energaticGwijo Squad…

V/O It was simply not our day.

Upsound Sijadu: We were almost there, but our defence wasn't where it should be. We lost.

Upsound Derek:The Gwijos never lost their voice

Upsound Sijadu : We never lost our voices

V/O … A fun-filled day spent with this group of sports lovers who believe fans should all sing with one voice.

[ end]
